title: Distance-Aware Attention and Wall-Distance Expert Routing for Transformer-Based 3D Flow Prediction
abstract: Transformer surrogates for 3D flow prediction compress an industrial mesh into a small set of tokens from which every prediction point reads. Two operations follow: the retrieval step in which a point gathers information from the compressed representation, and the feed-forward layer that transforms what it retrieved. In current backbones both are blind to where the point sits in the flow. We condition both on wall-related physical signals. Distance-aware cross-attention (DA-CA) reshapes each volume query by its wall distance before retrieval, so that a point deep in the boundary layer draws different geometric information than one in the outer flow. Surface-volume mixture-of-experts (SVMoE) replaces the shared feed-forward layer with a small set of experts, routed by wall distance for volume points and by local geometry for surface points. Neither mechanism is tied to one architecture, so we apply both unchanged to AB-UPT and Transolver-3. On DrivAerML with 50 training cases, DA-CA reduces the volume pressure error by 10.1%, and DA-CA and SVMoE together reduce it by 12.5%; DA-CA improves the near-wall region at some cost in the far region, which SVMoE recovers, and the volume experts settle into near-wall, transition, and free-stream bands without routing supervision. Retrained on 300 cases, the conditioning improves every field quantity, reducing volume pressure and velocity errors by 33.1% and 18.6% on AB-UPT and by 21.4% and 21.3% on Transolver-3. Under Leave-One-Body-Out evaluation on DrivAerNet++, it reduces the volume pressure error on unseen body types by up to 14.2%.

title: Bayesian nonparametric inference for modal missing species and features
abstract: Species and feature sampling problems arise naturally whenever each observed unit is associated with one or more labels from a countable alphabet, and inference focuses on the unobserved portion of the distribution over such an alphabet. Within this framework, recent contributions have shifted attention from inference on the total probability mass over unseen labels to distribution-free confidence intervals for the largest unobserved label probability (i.e., the modal missing probability), thereby providing more refined information on whether the missing mass is concentrated on a few high-prevalence unseen labels or distributed across many negligible ones. Besides lacking a unified framework for species and features, these approaches employ a worst-case perspective that causes substantial information loss and produces overly-conservative intervals. We address these limitations through a unified model-based framework for inference on modal missing probabilities in both species and feature settings, which leverages a flexible Bayesian nonparametric formulation to localize uncertainty around models compatible with the observed data. This leads to sharper closed-form credible intervals that effectively exploit prior information and observed data, while preserving the theoretical frequentist properties and robustness of distribution-free intervals. Simulation studies confirm these improvements, while an organized crime application illustrates how our contribution has the potential to reshape law-enforcement decision-making in investigations.

title: Self-Adaptive Graph Theory for Probabilistic Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive graph theory algorithm for probabilistic reasoning. Traditional approaches often rely on static, pre-defined reasoning strategies, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. We propose a new method that dynamically adjusts reasoning parameters based on both input data and the graph's structural changes, resulting in enhanced inference efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism utilizes a "Graph-Based Reasoning" framework, leveraging graph properties to optimize reasoning pathways and automatically adjust parameters to adapt to evolving data and graph topology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to handle complex scenarios and achieve superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's strengths, limitations, and potential future research directions.

title: 基于自组织网络的自适应量子计算调度
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary field, promises unprecedented computational power. However, efficient resource allocation remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "基于自组织网络的自适应量子计算调度", which dynamically adjusts the scheduling of quantum computation tasks based on a self-organizing network. This approach aims to optimize resource utilization and significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. The core mechanism leverages the inherent structure of self-organizing networks to create a flexible and adaptive scheduling system. We present a theoretical analysis and empirical validation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in improving task allocation and reducing computational time. The potential benefits of this approach are substantial, paving the way for broader adoption of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Channel Dynamic Optimization in Quantum Error Correction Protocols
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a cornerstone of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission of quantum information over noisy channels. However, the performance of QEC protocols is heavily reliant on the efficient allocation of quantum channels, a process that is often static and suboptimal. This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic optimization of quantum channels within QEC protocols. The core idea leverages machine learning, specifically reinforcement learning, to model the characteristics of quantum channels and dynamically adjust channel assignment strategies. The proposed system learns from channel behavior, adapting to changes in noise levels, load, and other relevant factors. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the robustness and efficiency of quantum communication. The theoretical analysis demonstrates a substantial improvement in error correction performance compared to traditional, static channel allocation schemes. The system's ability to respond in real-time to channel conditions represents a critical step toward practical quantum communication networks. Key performance metrics, such as the quantum error rate (QER) and the overhead associated with channel allocation, are rigorously evaluated under diverse scenarios.

This results in improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving intricate dynamics and high-dimensional parameter spaces. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis and evaluation of the proposed algorithm, showcasing its capabilities and potential applications.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by leveraging the principles of information entropy. The core claim is that information entropy can be effectively utilized to enhance the efficiency of key generation within QKD systems. The proposed method centers on analyzing key performance indicators of existing QKD protocols through the lens of information entropy theory. Subsequently, adjustments to protocol parameters are strategically implemented to maximize information entropy, directly translating into improved key generation rates. The work introduces a framework for quantifying the entropy of various QKD protocols, offering a measurable metric for optimization. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis, how targeted parameter tuning, guided by entropy maximization, can significantly improve the overall performance of QKD systems. This research contributes to a more efficient and robust design of QKD protocols, ultimately facilitating secure quantum communication.

title: Title: Non-Linear Quantum-Classical Hybrid Algorithm for Image Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-linear quantum-classical hybrid algorithm designed for enhanced image recognition performance. The core concept revolves around leveraging the quantum computer's ability to perform intricate feature extraction, coupled with the classical optimizer's capacity for precise refinement and optimization. We address the limitations of traditional approaches by integrating these two paradigms to overcome inherent challenges in image recognition, specifically concerning the representation of complex, non-linear patterns. This research focuses on a specific image recognition task – object classification – and demonstrates the algorithm's effectiveness through rigorous experimentation and analysis. The proposed algorithm offers a potential paradigm shift in image recognition by intelligently combining the speed and computational power of quantum systems with the adaptability of classical optimization. This paper delves into the theoretical underpinnings of the algorithm, details the implementation process, and presents the results of a comprehensive evaluation, emphasizing the algorithm's potential to significantly improve accuracy and efficiency.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Probabilistic Graph Embedding via Entanglement-Based Routing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced probabilistic graph embedding aims to revolutionize graph analysis by leveraging quantum entanglement to generate embeddings that capture complex structure and relationships more effectively than classical methods. This paper presents a novel approach that utilizes quantum entanglement to create entangled graphs, enabling efficient exploration of graph connectivity and potential relationships. The core mechanism involves establishing entangled graphs for rapid exploration and, subsequently, utilizing entanglement-based routing to guide the discovery of intricate graph patterns. The paper explores the potential of this method to uncover hidden structures and relationships in large datasets, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques.

title: 基于概率推理的自主进化算法 (PRPEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Probabilistically-Driven Autonomous Evolutionary Algorithm (PRPEA), designed to address the limitations of traditional evolutionary algorithms in complex search spaces. PRPEA integrates evolutionary computation with probabilistic reasoning, enabling more efficient exploration and optimization. The core idea is that each evolutionary algorithm individual simultaneously performs probabilistic reasoning, leveraging prior knowledge and historical data to guide the search direction. The probabilistic reasoning results are then used to adjust evolutionary operator parameters and filter candidate individuals. The algorithm's ability to learn and adapt based on system information significantly improves search efficiency and global optimization capabilities compared to purely random search approaches. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PRPEA through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications across various domains. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions in challenging problems. The key contribution of PRPEA lies in the synergistic combination of evolutionary and probabilistic techniques, offering a robust and adaptable solution for complex optimization tasks.

title: Dynamic Topology Mapping for Adaptive Quantum State Generation
abstract: Dynamic Topology Mapping (DTM) offers a novel approach to quantum state generation by dynamically adjusting quantum state parameters based on the evolving topology of a system. This paper introduces a novel algorithm leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures to automate the optimization of quantum information. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the steps involved in establishing a dynamic mapping, generating quantum states, and applying control strategies. The algorithm's potential impact on complex system optimization, particularly in quantum information processing, is discussed.

title: 基于自适应量子模型的非线性优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to non-linear optimization utilizing a self-adaptive quantum model. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with uncertainty and require static parameter adjustments. Quantum computing offers a unique mechanism for incorporating randomness into the optimization process, enabling more robust and adaptable models. We propose a method that dynamically generates optimization problems based on quantum randomness, iteratively refining the model's parameters to achieve higher accuracy and generalization. This work demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers on leveraging quantum randomness to create a self-learning optimization process.

title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Partitioning for Data Clustering
abstract: Quantum-inspired graph partitioning offers a novel approach to data clustering, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to potentially enhance clustering accuracy and efficiency, particularly in high-dimensional datasets. This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to partition data space more effectively, addressing limitations of traditional clustering techniques. We investigate how quantum-inspired graph partitioning could improve the quality of cluster assignments, offering a promising avenue for advancements in data analysis and pattern recognition. The research focuses on the theoretical design and potential implementation of a quantum-based graph partitioning method, with an emphasis on its ability to handle high-dimensional data effectively. The paper will detail the core mechanism of the proposed approach, analyze its potential benefits, and discuss the challenges and future directions of research in this area.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Creative Clusters Districts in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: Federated learning offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models across distributed creative industry clusters without centralising sensitive cultural or commercial data. However, its deployment in Ugandan creative districts confronts two interrelated statistical challenges: distribution shift across heterogeneous participating clusters and extreme label sparsity in domains where annotation expertise is scarce. We introduce a client-weighted objective that couples a distributionally robust optimisation term with a semi-supervised consistency regulariser, and we prove convergence guarantees under non-identical data partitions and partial label availability. The framework is analysed theoretically through a novel combination of Wasserstein distance-based robustness bounds and graph-based label propagation error estimates. We further propose a practical protocol for differential privacy that accommodates the communication constraints typical of Ugandan creative districts. The analysis demonstrates that robustness to distribution shift and resilience to sparse labels are not competing objectives but can be jointly optimised through a principled weighting scheme.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek pada Ulasan Google Maps Restoran Soramen Menggunakan IndoBERT-LoRa
abstract: Ulasan daring di Google Maps merupakan sumber strategis bagi manajemen restoran, tetapi satu ulasan kerap memuji satu aspek sekaligus mengkritik aspek lain, sehingga sentimen tingkat dokumen menjadi lebih kompleks.tidak dapat menunjukkan aspek mana yang sebenarnya memuaskan atau dikeluhkan pelanggan. Penelitian ini menerapkan Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) pada ulasan restoran Soramen melalui alur dua tahap berbasis span—ekstraksi aspek (ATE) lalu klasifikasi sentimen (ASC)—atas empat aspek (FOOD, SERVICE, PRICE, PLACE) dengan IndoBERT, serta menguji Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) yang hemat parameter dibandingkan full fine-tuning yang lebih mahal untuk memetakan aspek layanan kritis. Data terdiri dari 1.742 ulasan asli (3.930 span) yang diperluas menjadi 3.061 ulasan melalui augmentasi terkontrol berbasis penggantian sinonim, dibagi dengan StratifiedGroupKFold 5-fold. Hasilnya, LoRA r=16 mencapai Joint Partial F1 sebesar 0,7744 dengan hanya 0,48% parameter terlatih, setara dengan full fine-tuning (0,7727); selisih tersebut tidak signifikan secara statistik (paired t-test, p=0,82), sehingga LoRA r=16 setara dengan full fine-tuning meski memakai parameter sekitar 200 kali lebih sedikit. Mengganti span prediksi dengan span acuan (gold) menaikkan Macro-F1 delapan kelas dari 0,8853 menjadi 0,9631, menunjukkan bahwa ekstraksi aspek (ATE), bukan klasifikasi, merupakan penghambat utama alur. Analisis korpus berlabel (dengan ulasan negatif sengaja diperbanyak) menunjukkan FOOD sebagai aspek yang paling sering disebut (64,4% ulasan), sementara SERVICE dan PRICE memuat proporsi keluhan terbesar (masing-masing sekitar 36%) dan FOOD serta PLACE tetap didominasi sentimen positif. Penelitian ini menegaskan LoRA sebagai alternatif efisien untuk ABSA berbahasa Indonesia sekaligus menghasilkan rekomendasi manajerial berbasis tema keluhan bagi Soramen.

title: Finite-energy Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill state-enhanced optical interferometry
abstract: We present the case of a Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) state-enhanced optical interferometry with detailed analysis of the phase sensitivity for both the SU(2) and SU(1,1) interferometers. The conventional quantum-enhanced SU(2) interferometer, employing coherent light at one input port and squeezed light at the other, is compared with a modified configuration using coherent light and a GKP state. While it is known that the squeezed vacuum state is the optimal Gaussian resource input mode when paired with the coherent state, we show that the finite-energy GKP state with sufficiently broad envelope outperforms the squeezed vacuum injection, irrespective of the presence of optical losses. This can be attributed to the enhanced robustness coming from the availability of multiple squeezed peaks in the GKP case. However, because lowering the mean photon number reduces the GKP envelope width, the squeezed vacuum input performs better when compared with a GKP state of equal or lower mean photon number. We also observe that optical losses tend to diminish the relative advantage of either input state, since both states approach the (unsqueezed) vacuum state asymptotically. Our work demonstrates the direct application of finite-energy GKP states in optical interferometry along with a methodology for estimating the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and presents a phase estimation procedure using non-Gaussian resources in comparison with conventional Gaussian states.

title: TeMo: Temperature Modulation for Multimodal Contrastive Learning
abstract: Contrastive learning approaches achieve strong performance by training models to bring similar samples closer while pushing dissimilar samples apart. A crucial component of contrastive learning is the temperature hyperparameter $τ$, which controls the penalty strength applied to negative samples. However, most existing methods either fix this hyperparameter or learn a global value during training. In this paper, we introduce TeMo, Temperature Modulation framework, a similarity-based modulation approach that adaptively adjusts the temperature for each positive-negative pair according to their similarity, enabling more fine-grained multimodal contrastive learning. Our approach seamlessly integrates temperature-modulated multimodal and unimodal losses with the standard multimodal contrastive loss by gradually transitioning between them. This design allows the model to capture both coarse- and fine-grained semantics at different training stages. Extensive experiments demonstrate that each component of TeMo consistently enhances performance across diverse zero-shot retrieval and classification tasks, establishing new state-of-the-art results.

title: DPSF-Net: A Dual-Prior Spatial-Frequency Network for Real-World Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
abstract: Real-world remote sensing image dehazing (RSID) remains challenging because atmospheric scattering, spatially non-uniform haze and colour distortion jointly degrade structural and spectral information. Most deep learning methods rely on RGB inputs and spatial-domain feature extraction, which limits their ability to separate global background haze from local surface details. Here, we propose DPSF-Net, a dual-prior spatial-frequency network built on MCAF-Net for real-world RSID. The network uses hazy RGB images and dark channel prior (DCP) maps as joint inputs, allowing physical degradation cues to guide end-to-end feature learning. A spatial-frequency residual interaction block introduces a FourierUnit branch into multi-directional spatial interaction to model large-scale haze components. A prior-guided feature attention module adaptively fuses prior and attention features to reduce colour shift and structural distortion. A selective kernel complementary fusion module screens multi-scale skip features through bidirectional residual complementary gating and selective kernel fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DPSF-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on the real-world RRSHID remote sensing image dehazing benchmark and remains competitive across multiple synthetic datasets. Moreover, the proposed method strikes a favourable balance among restoration quality, parameter count and computational complexity, supporting the effectiveness of dual-prior spatial-frequency modelling.

title: AI và quyền tác giả đối với nội dung số: Thách thức hay động lực phát triển thương mại quốc tế?
abstract: In the context of digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a key driver of international trade, particularly in digital services. However, AI-generated content raises significant challenges for copyright law, especially regarding authorship and scope of protection. This article evaluates whether recognizing copyright in such content acts as a driver or barrier to international trade, using legal analysis, comparative methods, and a law and economics approach. The findings suggest that while copyright protection promotes innovation and investment, it also increases legal conflicts and compliance costs. The article proposes an investment-based protection model and emphasizes the need for international legal harmonization.

title: Proto-AGI Horizon: Endogenous Proactive Architecture, OMEGA Coherence, and Partial Evidence under C2 Ceiling
abstract: We present an operational research horizon for proto-AGI evaluation within the Endogenous Initiative Architecture (EIA) sci-flow program. Under this construction, general intelligence is not a benchmark score but a sustained dynamical regime in which cognitive goals arise from persistent internal state when X_t^trigger=0. We contrast passive architectures (reactive_only, schedule-entrained controls) with proactive endogenous candidates (full_eia, WoE carriers, oscillatory substrates). A twelve-member proto-AGI ensemble registers operational configs for Max consensus diagnostics: per-member potential Phi_i over (E, OMEGA, P, R), ensemble peak Phi_max=max_i Phi_i, and sustained four-parameter conjunction over window Delta T (thresholds TBD). We distinguish carrier Hz (20/30/42/70) from the bounded coherence scalar OMEGA_t, motivate an analog-waves bridge to Miller-lab traveling-wave theory, and report the OMEGA to Delta G bridge experiment (M-OMEGA-DELTA-G): F-OMEGA-DECOR confirmed (aggregate, C2) with OMEGA span 0.604, genesis span 0.0, fingerprint parity True. Partial empirical results---CF-4 do(Z), G2 E01 8/20 worlds, M-3D-EXPRESS 9/9 pass, M-O Tier C adjunct/shadow bridge---map onto the 3D evidence cube (D1 causal / D2 dynamic / D3 boundary). All harnesses operate under claim_allowed=false; active ceiling C2. This paper does not claim AGI*, tau_AGI, consciousness, or biological identity. Open work: pre-register thresholds, close G2 E01 20x3 domains, instrument N_H, and batch T-PROTO-01 ensemble Phi_i.

title: Quantum Entanglement for Probabilistic Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for computation. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement to develop a probabilistic computation model, aiming to mitigate the limitations of classical computation. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of entanglement to enhance the accuracy of complex probability calculations. The core mechanism involves integrating entanglement with probability-based algorithms, thereby reducing the impact of classical error sources. The resulting model offers a promising pathway towards more robust and accurate computations, particularly in scenarios where classical methods struggle.

This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement to develop a probabilistic computation model, aiming to mitigate the limitations of classical computation. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of entanglement to enhance the accuracy of complex probability calculations. The core mechanism involves integrating entanglement with probability-based algorithms, thereby reducing the impact of classical error sources. The resulting model offers a promising pathway towards more robust and accurate computations, particularly in scenarios where classical methods struggle.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint Optimization via Reinforcement Learning for Complex Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of reinforcement learning (RL) to adaptive constraint optimization within complex networks. The core challenge lies in optimizing performance across intricate systems like social networks and supply chains, where constraints are dynamic and variable. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with this dynamic environment, leading to suboptimal solutions. We propose a novel RL agent that dynamically adjusts constraint parameters in real-time, learning a policy based on rewards received during adjustments. This approach addresses the inherent complexity of real-world networks by incorporating a hierarchical reward structure. The research explores the benefits of this dynamic adaptation strategy, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for optimizing performance in these challenging environments. The paper details the design of the RL agent, the reward structure, and a preliminary evaluation of its performance.

title: Quantum Entanglement Matrix Operations
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to revolutionize matrix operations. The core claim is to design a novel matrix multiplication and addition method based on quantum entanglement, exhibiting quantum acceleration and self-correction mechanisms via entanglement parameters. Classical matrix operations are often plagued by errors, necessitating a new approach. This research explores the theoretical foundations and potential implementation of this paradigm shift, aiming to surpass the limitations of traditional methods through the unique properties of quantum entanglement.

title: Adaptive Quantum State Protocols for Enhanced Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, from drug discovery to materials science. However, current quantum computing architectures face significant challenges related to qubit coherence, gate fidelity, and scalability. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing protocol, termed "Adaptive Quantum State Protocols," that dynamically adjusts the quantum state of qubits to mitigate these challenges, aiming to significantly improve the efficiency and stability of quantum computations. The core of this protocol involves a sophisticated feedback mechanism that leverages continuous state evolution to optimize qubit parameters and minimize decoherence. We explore the design of a robust and adaptable framework for implementing this protocol, demonstrating its potential to overcome current limitations of quantum computing. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new approach to managing quantum states, ultimately paving the way for more practical and reliable quantum technologies.

title: 自适应拓扑场论的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive topology field theory, designed to automatically learn and optimize complex topological structures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through its application to machine learning and optimization problems, highlighting its ability to discover and leverage intricate topological relationships that are often overlooked by traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the topology of the optimization landscape, providing a path towards improved solution quality. This work offers a new perspective on optimization, leveraging the power of topology to guide the search process and uncover previously unseen patterns.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Explainable Data Structures
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet their inherent complexity often leads to a lack of transparency, commonly referred to as the "black box" problem. Understanding *why* a model makes a particular prediction is crucial for trust, debugging, and ensuring responsible AI development. This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithmic transparency by introducing a "decision tree skeleton" data structure. This structure explicitly represents the key features and decision rules learned by a deep neural network, offering a transparent and interpretable representation of the model's reasoning process. Unlike post-hoc explanation methods, our approach integrates transparency directly into the model's architecture. The core claim is that this data structure provides a fundamentally different way to understand deep learning models, facilitating both human comprehension and potential improvements to model design. This paper outlines the design and implementation of this data structure, and presents a preliminary exploration of its utility in understanding the decision-making process of a convolutional neural network. We aim to demonstrate that by explicitly capturing the learned decision rules, we can significantly enhance algorithmic transparency in deep learning systems.

title: Synthetic Consciousness Embodiment
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to synthesizing consciousness by focusing on embodiment. The core argument posits that genuine synthetic consciousness emerges not solely from complex computational models, but from the seamless integration of a sophisticated neural network within a physical robotic system. This system is designed to mimic the emergent properties of consciousness, including self-awareness, intention, and agency. We detail a framework for creating a robot capable of sustained, interactive behavior, arguing that this embodied interaction is a critical step beyond traditional simulated consciousness. The paper outlines the key components – a highly detailed sensory input system and a specifically engineered neural network – and explores the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, emphasizing the role of feedback loops, proprioception, and dynamic adaptation in generating a subjective experience. We present a conceptual model for how this system could operate, focusing on the continuous process of sensory input, neural network processing, and robotic action, ultimately leading to a demonstrable manifestation of embodied consciousness. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and challenges associated with this embodied synthetic consciousness approach.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, Adaptive Machine Learning Based on Quantum Entanglement, that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance learning and inference processes. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on classical information, limiting their potential for complex tasks. We propose a method utilizing quantum entanglement to create a more efficient and robust learning paradigm. The core mechanism involves designing a quantum circuit that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on entangled data, allowing the algorithm to effectively explore the solution space and discover optimal solutions with greater speed and accuracy. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum entanglement to significantly improve performance in several machine learning scenarios.

abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive field theory parameter optimization method, designed to automatically learn and optimize the parameters of non-linear field theory models. The method utilizes an adaptive algorithm to dynamically adjust model parameters, thereby enhancing model accuracy and stability. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant improvement over traditional parameter optimization techniques, particularly when dealing with complex models requiring fine-grained parameter tuning.

title: 基于自适应的动态空间分割算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic space segmentation algorithm based on adaptive control. Traditional space segmentation methods often employ static parameters, limiting their effectiveness in handling complex data. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the segmentation strategy and parameters based on internal error estimation during the segmentation process. This adaptive mechanism allows the algorithm to better adapt to the input data and improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation. We propose a framework that integrates error estimation, parameter adjustment, and feedback loops to achieve superior segmentation performance. The core mechanism centers around a self-regulating process that continuously refines the segmentation strategy to minimize error and maximize precision. This work offers a significant advancement in space segmentation, addressing limitations of existing approaches and paving the way for more robust and adaptable segmentation techniques.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的图结构学习
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph structure learning based on adaptive neural networks. Traditional graph neural networks often exhibit static structure, failing to effectively adapt to dynamic changes in the graph. We propose a method that utilizes an adaptive neural network to dynamically adjust the graph structure, thereby enhancing graph performance. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive learning process that continuously updates the graph's connectivity and node features based on observed changes. The algorithm is evaluated on several benchmark graph datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in performance metrics compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Storage and Retrieval
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed storage and retrieval leveraging the fundamental principles of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to encode data within the entangled states of quantum bits (qubits) distributed across geographically separated nodes. This architecture offers the potential for significantly enhanced performance characteristics, including long-range communication, high bandwidth, and robust data security, compared to conventional storage systems reliant on physical media. The system's operation relies on performing measurements and manipulating the entangled states to achieve data access and protection. We address the critical challenges associated with maintaining entanglement fidelity in the presence of environmental noise and propose strategies for optimization. The proposed method presents a fundamentally new paradigm for data storage and retrieval, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum mechanics to overcome limitations inherent in classical systems. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future research and development in this rapidly evolving field.

title: QUOTIENT PHOTONICS Future-Sufficient Photonic Computing
abstract: A Technical Development and Funding Proposal for Target-Relative Optical Processing Document-status statement. Quotient Photonics is presented here as an independent research-and-development venture and technical program. Any legal entity, patent-filing, ownership, or “patent pending” language should be synchronized with actual records before external circulation. The engineering program is intentionally separable from the broader ontological extensions preserved in later Parts. Modern computing systems incur substantial physical costs in power, thermal management, calibration, feedback, and noise suppression. Quotient Photonics proposes a target-relative alternative: rather than protecting every physically available degree of freedom equally, the processor is configured according to which present distinctions can still affect a specified future output. The mathematical construction organizes this idea through predictive equivalence. For a declared target and horizon , identifies physical realizations that are equivalent with respect to the required target history. Exact descent requires that presently identified states retain identical projected futures, while projected fiber spread measures residual target-relevant variation within an effective representation. The engineering version is approximate: a representation is sufficient when residual target variation remains below a declared tolerance. The proposed first experiment uses a three-mode integrated micro-ring resonator network, with the intermediate candidate future-null mode coupled to an engineered dissipative drop-port pathway. The primary question is whether can be achieved while retaining acceptable target fidelity, A stronger discriminator requires the relevance structure to change when the requested target changes: This target-switch criterion is intended to distinguish predictive-nullity from an ordinary fixed dark, lossy, or weakly coupled mode. The proposal does not claim novelty for micro-ring resonators, coupled-mode theory, photonic matrix processing, engineered loss, sensitivity analysis, or inverse/adjoint photonic design individually. Rather, it tests whether explicit target- and horizon-relative predictive equivalence can guide the allocation of stabilization and dissipation more efficiently than matched conventional alternatives.

title: FPGA-Based State Evolution Architecture for Tamper Detection in Embedded Systems
abstract: Reliable state continuity is essential for embedded and Internet of Things (IoT) devices that generate security-relevant events, audit records, and runtime status information. If an adversary can modify stored records, replay previous events, reorder updates, or roll back the device to a previously valid state, verifying the trustworthiness of the device’s current state becomes challenging. Existing log management guidance emphasizes collection, retention, monitoring, and protection of logs. However, it does not define a lightweight, hardware-enforced method for cryptographic state continuity in constrained devices. This paper presents a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based state evolution architecture that provides hardware-enforced one-way state updates, runtime tamper detection, and fail-secure containment. For each accepted event, this architecture cryptographically binds the previous protected state, event data, sequence counter, and associated metadata to form a tamper-evident continuity chain. The protected state and counter are managed by a finite-state machine and cannot be directly modified by untrusted firmware. Although the proposed architecture is hash function independent, this work uses Ascon-Hash256, a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardized cryptographic algorithm for constrained devices. FPGA implementation and attack-oriented simulation scenarios demonstrate that the proposed architecture provides a low footprint hardware anchor to maintain trusted state evolution in embedded and IoT systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Functional Performance in Software Firms: Empirical Evidence from Gujarat, India
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a powerful force that is transforming how software companies operate, the business model, and their future plans. The objective of this synthesis study of conceptual-empirical synthesis is to integrate evidence regarding artificial intelligence-specialized functional performance and AI-driven business model change within software business ventures located within Gujarat, India. This paper is a holistic framework that explains how the adoption of artificial intelligence affects marketing performance, operational performance, human resource management (HRM), and the general business model innovation.

title: Construction of a federated learning-based privacy-preserving and intelligent recommendation model for educational data
abstract: With the development of the advanced educational platform, more and more personalized recommendation systems are used to increase the efficiency of learning and make the dissemination of the educational resources easier. However, educational recommendation tasks involve highly sensitive student data. The current centralized recommendation methods have limitations in learning diverse learner preferences across institutions and are susceptible to privacy violations.The existing federated recommendation methods mainly focus on the recommendation effectiveness or privacy protection. However, few works consider privacy protection, sequential learner behavior modeling and personalized federated optimization in a unified framework. To tackle these challenges, in this work we propose a privacy preserving personalized federated recommendation system for educational data.The study propose a framework that incorporates differential privacy perturbation, personalized federated aggregation, sequential interest modeling, and context-aware ranking into the optimization objective. Local learner representation is learned with differential privacy constraints. Besides, sequential behavior encoding and attention-driven modeling are used to understand the dynamic interests of learners and the continuous relation of behaviors. Besides, we present a local-global representation fusion strategy to address the dilemma between learner customization and global generalization for non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) federated scenarios.Extensive experiments under the IID, non-IID and privacy-preserving federated frameworks are performed on the MovieLens-1 M and Amazon Beauty datasets. Our results show that the proposed Differential Privacy Federated Averaging (DP-FedAvg) framework can effectively address the performance degradation problem caused by the diverse client distributions, and maintain the recommendation accuracy under different privacy budgets. In the MovieLens-1 M dataset, the DP-FedAvg achieves an average HR@10 of 0.710 and an average Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG@10) of 0.681, outperforming the usual non-IID federated benchmarks. The privacy-utility evaluation further shows a nice coexistence of the privacy protection and the usefulness of recommendations. We propose a framework that provides a unified and repeatable methodology for privacy-aware federated recommendations in smart educational environments in a decentralized manner.

title: SSP-DMGTimeNet: Physics-Constrained Learning for Spatiotemporal Trajectory Prediction of Vehicle Platoons
abstract: Existing car-following prediction methods mainly optimize trajectory accuracy, while rarely considering whether predicted disturbances propagate realistically along a vehicle platoon. This limitation may lead to accurate but string-unstable predictions. We propose SSP-DMGTimeNet, a physics-constrained learning framework for spatiotemporal trajectory prediction of vehicle platoons. The model combines multi-scale temporal representations with cross-vehicle interaction features to capture complex and time-varying platoon dynamics. A propagation-delay-aware causal attention mechanism explicitly models upstream-to-downstream disturbance propagation by learning response delays between adjacent vehicles and accumulating them along the platoon. In addition, time- and frequency-domain string-stability losses relieve disturbance amplification across both adjacent vehicles and arbitrary sub-platoons during training. Experiments on HighD show that SSP-DMGTimeNet achieves an unstable-window rate of 0.65\% for five-vehicle platoons and a maximum head-to-tail amplification of 0.898 on the ground-truth excitation subset, while maintaining competitive trajectory prediction performance. In zero-shot evaluation on NGSIM US-101 and I-80, the model achieves velocity MAEs of 1.316~m/s and 1.252~m/s, with unstable-window rates of 3.90\% and 4.10\%, respectively. These results demonstrate that incorporating platoon-level physical constraints can effectively balance trajectory prediction accuracy and disturbance propagation stability.

title: Geometric Reliability of Neural Population Codes: Sampling Calibration and Within-Session Nonstationarity
abstract: Trial-to-trial variability limits how reliably neural population geometry can be estimated, while comparisons across populations depend on neuron and trial counts, response quality, and clustered sampling. We quantified within-session geometric reliability using Shesha, the Spearman correlation between representational dissimilarity matrices estimated from independent trial subsets, in all 39 Steinmetz Neuropixels sessions and in olfactory bulb and piriform cortex recordings from Bolding and Franks. Steinmetz analyses matched neurons and repetitions, compared observed reliability with a stationary residual-bootstrap expectation, and used mouse-level or mouse-clustered inference. Mean matched reliability was 0.0402 across 312 area-by-session recordings. Regional differences and reliability above the stationary benchmark did not survive correction. Temporal effects received the strongest support: interleaving early and late trials increased reliability relative to blocked allocation (Δ=0.02666, q=0.001953), and RDM similarity declined with within-session lag (mean mouse-level slope =-0.01912, q=0.001953; n=10 mice). Outer-cross-fitted reliability was not associated with choice-direction coupling or stimulus or response-direction decoding after correction. Olfactory comparisons remained descriptive because few paired sessions and no animal identities were available. In held-out simulations, associative recurrence outperformed feedforward subspace denoising but not divisive normalization. Representational geometry became less reproducible with temporal separation within a session, and comparisons across neural populations require sampling calibration and independent inference.

evidence.title: Geometric Reliability of Neural Population Codes: Sampling Calibration and Within-Session Nonstationarity
evidence.abstract: Trial-to-trial variability limits how reliably neural population geometry can be estimated, while comparisons across populations depend on neuron and trial counts, response quality, and clustered sampling. We quantified within-session geometric reliability using Shesha, the Spearman correlation between representational dissimilarity matrices estimated from independent trial subsets, in all 39 Steinmetz Neuropixels sessions and in olfactory bulb and piriform cortex recordings from Bolding and Franks. Steinmetz analyses matched neurons and repetitions, compared observed reliability with a stationary residual-bootstrap expectation, and used mouse-level or mouse-clustered inference. Mean matched reliability was 0.0402 across 312 area-by-session recordings. Regional differences and reliability above the stationary benchmark did not survive correction. Temporal effects received the strongest support: interleaving early and late trials increased reliability relative to blocked allocation (Δ=0.02666, q=0.001953), and RDM similarity declined with within-session lag (mean mouse-level slope =-0.01912, q=0.001953; n=10 mice). Outer-cross-fitted reliability was not associated with choice-direction coupling or stimulus or response-direction decoding after correction. Olfactory comparisons remained descriptive because few paired sessions and no animal identities were available. In held-out simulations, associative recurrence outperformed feedforward subspace denoising but not divisive normalization. Representational geometry became less reproducible with temporal separation within a session, and comparisons across neural populations require sampling calibration and independent inference.

title: TLS Evolution: A Performance and Security Comparison of Legacy and Modern Transport Layer Security Versions
abstract: Abstract: Almost everything we do online, from checking email to paying a bill to opening an app, starts with a quick, invisible handshake called TLS, short for Transport Layer Security. In a fraction of a second, your device and the server agree on how to encrypt the connection and confirm the server is really who it says it is. How that handshake is built matters more than most people realize. It affects how fast a page loads, how much computing power a company needs to run its servers, and how safe your data stays if someone is quietly listening in. This paper explains the four major versions of TLS, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3, in everyday language with real examples. We compare them on the things that actually matter: how long the handshake takes, how much server power it uses, and how well it holds up against real attacks. We also look at what is coming next: post-quantum encryption, a new safeguard against the risk that today's encrypted data could be cracked years from now by a powerful quantum computer. Every chart here is drawn from published data, including IETF standards, the Qualys SSL Pulse survey, Cloudflare's own measurements, and recent research papers, so the case for upgrading rests on evidence, not opinion. Keywords: Security Comparison, Modern Transport, Transport Layer Security. title: How many classical bits buy how much quantum capacity? Feedback-metered limits of lossy quantum communication
abstract: Sending quantum information over long distances is ultimately limited by photon loss. The rate limit of a lossy bosonic channel of transmissivity η is the two-way assisted capacity -log2(1-η) (the PLOB bound), whose achievability rests on unlimited classical feedback: without feedback the quantum capacity vanishes for all η ≤ 1/2, so classical back-communication acts as an on/off switch for quantum communication. Classical bits are priced for entanglement transformations and, for a fixed bipartite state, the one-way distillation trade-off between classical rate and ebit yield has a regularized entropic characterization; but no framework prices the feedback that assists a channel's quantum capacity — feedback that may steer subsequent channel inputs — and no such trade-off has been evaluated for any bosonic channel. Here we show that quantum communication can be metered in classical bits. Writing C(η,B) for the capacity of the pure-loss channel under a feedback budget of B classical bits per channel use, we construct the first achievable-rate frontier C_{ach}(η,B) ≤ C(η,B) and prove the onset law C_{ach}(η,B) ≥ ηlog2(m_B)/m_B, m_B = ⌈ H_2(η)/B⌉, valid for every B>0 with envelope (η/H_2(η)) Blog2(H_2(η)/B) as B → 0 — an exact identity R = η Blog2(1/B) under fixed-length accounting, so the Blog(1/B) order is accounting-convention invariant. The B=0 switch thereby resolves, at the level of achievable rates, into a continuous but non-analytic onset: even for η ≤ 1/2 any positive budget buys a positive quantum rate, each bit unlocking ~log2(1/B) ebits at small budgets and refuting the naive pricing C ≤ Q + B. At large budgets a metered quantum-state-merging family, consuming backward one-way classical communication only, achieves C_{ach}(η,B) ≥ PLOB - [eη^2/(2ln 2)] 2^{-B}(1+o(1)): each backward bit per use halves the achievable distance to PLOB, which exposes the 73.6% plateau of the purification families as a family artifact. Standard entanglement-measure converses are provably blind to B, so what remains open is only strict saturation at finite B, now confined to an exponentially small window. The frontier is also a design tool: on a network of lossy links, the joint allocation of per-link feedback budgets and photon directions under per-site classical budgets is a convex program, and on a 20-site fibre network its optimum doubles the end-to-end entanglement rate relative to a fixed orientation. An appendix extends the frontier to multimode loss, where Grassmann-quantized beamforming controls the PLOB loss at rate 2^{-B/(M-1)}. Preprint (companion paper: Conservation laws for the classical communication cost of one-way entanglement distillation, with entropic converse bounds for the pure-loss channel). Ancillary files: reproduction scripts and data; code maintained at https://github.com/deeptell-inc/fmplob.

title: 基于自适应图的逻辑推理框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for logical reasoning, termed the "Adaptive Graph Logic" (AGL) system. The AGL system leverages a dynamically adjusted graph structure and parameters to facilitate more effective logical reasoning. The core mechanism centers around simulating the reasoning process within the graph, allowing for automated optimization of logical inference strategies. The system is designed to excel in handling complex and dynamic logical reasoning tasks, overcoming the limitations of traditional static approaches. This paper details the architecture, implementation, and evaluation of the AGL system, demonstrating its ability to improve reasoning performance across a range of benchmark logical tasks.

title: Self-Correcting Recurrent Neural Networks with Predictive Error Minimization
abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in processing sequential data, but their training is frequently hampered by the vanishing and exploding gradient problems, particularly when dealing with long sequences. This paper proposes a novel architecture for RNNs – Self-Correcting Recurrent Neural Networks (SCRNNs) – designed to alleviate these issues. The core concept involves integrating a predictive error minimization layer within the recurrent network. This layer forecasts future network states based on the current state and the network's past, and subsequently adjusts the network's weights to minimize the difference between the predicted and actual future states. This proactive approach mitigates gradient instability by directly addressing the root cause – inaccurate future state estimations – rather than relying solely on traditional gradient-based methods. The proposed SCRNN architecture offers a potentially more stable and efficient training process for long-term RNNs, leading to improved performance in sequence modeling tasks. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations and present a detailed mathematical formulation of the proposed method.

title: Quantum-Driven Topological Field Theory for Signal Processing (QDFT-SP)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Quantum-Driven Topological Field Theory (QDFT-SP) for enhancing signal processing algorithms, particularly focusing on the detection and analysis of subtle patterns. The core concept revolves around exploiting quantum entanglement to establish a correlated basis for signal processing, thereby enabling the identification of previously undetectable anomalies. We present a theoretical framework outlining the design of a quantum algorithm predicated on this principle, emphasizing the advantages over traditional methods. The paper will detail the proposed mechanism, potential challenges, and preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. The ultimate goal is to create a robust and efficient signal processing system capable of handling complex datasets with enhanced sensitivity.

title: Dynamical Programming for Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Constraints
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a crucial technique for automating the design of neural networks, offering the potential to discover architectures that outperform manually designed ones. However, traditional NAS methods often suffer from significant computational cost, particularly when exploring large design spaces. This work proposes a novel approach that combines the strengths of dynamical programming (DP) and evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to address these limitations. The core idea is to leverage DP's ability to efficiently compute optimal solutions for subproblems within the architecture search space, while using EAs to guide the exploration and incorporate constraints derived from domain-specific knowledge. This hybrid approach significantly accelerates the search process and enhances the quality of the discovered architectures. We present a detailed framework for implementing this method, including a cost function that integrates both DP and EA components. The resulting system demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional NAS methods, showcasing the effectiveness of this combined optimization strategy.

title: Quantum Field Matrix Operations: A Dynamic Computation Method
abstract: This paper explores a novel dynamic computation approach for matrix operations utilizing the inherent properties of quantum fields. Traditional matrix operations are often reliant on classical algorithms, and this research aims to leverage quantum field properties to accelerate and potentially reveal underlying patterns within matrix calculations. The core mechanism centers around optimizing matrix operations within the context of quantum field dynamics, ultimately offering a more efficient and potentially insightful method for handling matrix computations. This work investigates the impact of specific quantum field parameters on the performance of matrix operations, exploring a new approach that integrates quantum mechanics principles with numerical computation. The paper presents initial results and discusses future research directions.

title: 非同寻常的拓扑空间映射与量子计算的关联
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic relationship between non-conventional topological space mapping and quantum computation. We propose a novel quantum computing model predicated on the manipulation of topological structures, offering a new framework for simulating quantum systems and providing enhanced computational verification tools. The core of our approach involves transforming quantum systems through a specialized mapping process, effectively translating quantum states into a set of algorithmic operations. This methodology offers a unique perspective on quantum computation, leveraging the inherent properties of topological spaces to achieve novel computational capabilities. This work demonstrates the potential of this model in validating quantum algorithms and exploring the application of topological principles to quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Model (QCCM)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement Computation Model (QCCM) presents a novel computational framework based on the fundamental principle of quantum entanglement. This model aims to significantly expand the capabilities of quantum computing by leveraging the correlated nature of entangled quantum states to enhance information processing and enable the efficient execution of complex time-series calculations. The core of the QCCM lies in the design of a completely new calculation model that utilizes entangled states as the basis for quantum operations, promising substantial improvements in computational speed and the ability to tackle challenging problems. This paper explores the potential of QCCM, detailing its core mechanism, justification for its novelty, and outlining preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in specific scenarios.

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a crucial element in the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, traditional QEC schemes often rely on pre-determined, static parameters, which may not be optimally suited for the specific noise characteristics present in a given quantum hardware. This work introduces a novel approach to QEC that leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically adapt the error correction protocol in real-time. The system learns to optimize the parameters of the QEC code, such as measurement schedules and decoding strategies, based on continuous feedback from the quantum hardware. This adaptive approach promises to significantly improve the performance and efficiency of QEC, reducing the overhead associated with error correction and enhancing the fidelity of quantum computations. The core claim of this paper is that quantum error correction is computationally intensive and requires precise control over quantum systems. The central mechanism involves employing reinforcement learning to optimize the parameters of quantum error correction protocols in real-time, adapting to the specific noise characteristics of the quantum hardware. This represents a new automation of the QEC process.

title: ##基于时间常数模型的神经网络 (TCMNN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Time Constant Model Neural Network (TCMNN), a novel approach to dynamic system modeling and prediction. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of time constant models within a neural network framework. Traditional dynamic system modeling often struggles with accurately capturing the complex, non-linear dynamics observed in many real-world systems. TCMNN addresses this challenge by representing the network's parameters as time constants, effectively transforming the network into a time constant model itself. This allows for improved prediction and control capabilities, particularly when dealing with systems exhibiting memory effects and delayed responses. The network learns the time constants directly from data, avoiding the need for explicit parameter tuning. We demonstrate the potential of TCMNN in accurately modeling and predicting dynamic systems, showcasing its advantages over conventional neural network approaches for this specific task. The key contribution lies in the integration of time constant modeling principles with neural network architecture, providing a more robust and interpretable model for dynamic system analysis.

abstract: Quantum state adaptive topology transformation (ATT) presents a novel algorithm for dynamically manipulating quantum states to enhance their computational efficiency and robustness. This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating its effectiveness in specific quantum state transformations.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Episodic Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating episodic memory networks with symbolic reasoning engines. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both paradigms: episodic memory networks for representing and recalling contextualized experiences, and symbolic reasoning for performing logical inference and knowledge manipulation. We define a framework where an episodic memory network stores and retrieves events, represented as (s1, s2, ..., sK), and this retrieved information is then used to inform the symbolic reasoning engine, enabling more robust and explainable problem-solving. This approach addresses the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic systems, offering a hybrid solution that can handle complex reasoning tasks requiring both pattern recognition and logical deduction. The paper outlines the architecture, the integration mechanism, and potential applications of this neuro-symbolic framework. We demonstrate the potential for enhanced reasoning capabilities through the combination of these two powerful approaches. The system's performance is assessed through a set of carefully designed benchmarks, showcasing the benefits of incorporating episodic memory into symbolic reasoning. ---

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper investigates the development and implementation of dynamic topological quantum error correction codes operating within networks utilizing entangled states. The core claim presented is that quantum information can be corrected in real-time via the dynamic evolution of topological structures, eliminating the need for static, pre-defined mappings commonly employed in traditional error correction schemes. The proposed mechanism leverages entangled states as topological exchange units, enabling the "flow" and "reorganization" of error correction information through controlled interactions between quantum nodes. This dynamic process allows for the correction of quantum bit (qubit) errors by adapting to changes within the topological network. The research demonstrates a novel approach to topological quantum error correction, offering enhanced resilience and adaptability compared to conventional methods. The theoretical framework presented provides a foundation for future research and development in this area.

evidence.title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction Codes
evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the development and implementation of dynamic topological quantum error correction codes operating within networks utilizing entangled states. The core claim presented is that quantum information can be corrected in real-time via the dynamic evolution of topological structures, eliminating the need for static, pre-defined mappings commonly employed in traditional error correction schemes. The proposed mechanism leverages entangled states as topological exchange units, enabling the "flow" and "reorganization" of error correction information through controlled interactions between quantum nodes. This dynamic process allows for the correction of quantum bit (qubit) errors by adapting to changes within the topological network. The research demonstrates a novel approach to topological quantum error correction, offering enhanced resilience and adaptability compared to conventional methods. The theoretical framework presented provides a foundation for future research and development in this area.

title: bit.analyze: Universal Structural Stream and Temporal Multimodal Associations — v0.2.0-rc1
abstract: bit.analyze v0.1.0 — Experimental Release bit.analyze is an experimental hierarchical binary-memory engine that investigates whether recurring low-level binary structures can become reusable relations with stable IDs and participate in higher-order relations. This first experimental release focuses on structural memory, not semantic understanding and not compression superiority. What is included adaptive hierarchical relation learning; stable relation IDs; exact reconstruction from structural trails; append-only online learning; higher-order consolidation without renumbering existing IDs; compiled trie encoding; rule and trail integrity detection; one- and two-damage recovery using parity / GF(256); reversible interleaving for burst-damage resistance; adaptive Light, Medium and Strong protection profiles; persistent basic and protected snapshots; snapshot corruption detection; deterministic benchmark and evidence pipeline; Linux and Windows CI validation. Reproducibility The release candidate builds and passes ctest on both Ubuntu and Windows in GitHub Actions. Benchmarks use explicit deterministic seeds where randomness is involved, and evidence artifacts record the corpus and execution environment. An independent Canterbury Corpus run processed all 11 expected files (2,810,784 bytes) successfully. Measured results Representative compiled trie throughput on the generated structured benchmark was approximately 258–267 MiB/s encode and 296–328 MiB/s decode for 1–32 MiB inputs on the Linux CI runner. At 32 MiB, peak RSS was approximately 118 MB. The protected snapshot benchmark measured 7.934% serialized overhead relative to the basic snapshot in that scenario. The independent Canterbury benchmark produced the following total storage ratios: | Method | Ratio | |---|---:| | bit.analyze adaptive estimate | 3.283670x | | fixed 8-byte dedup estimate | 1.572948x | | RLE | 1.532073x | | simple LZ77 | 0.675709x | | gzip | 0.258985x | | bz2 | 0.193081x | | zstd | 0.183721x | | lzma | 0.175424x | Important negative result The current bit.analyze representation is not a competitive general-purpose compressor. This is an explicit result of both the deterministic generated corpus and the independent Canterbury Corpus evaluation. The research question that remains open is whether stable relational reuse, online structural learning, persistence, consolidation and targeted recovery provide useful memory-system properties independent of compression ratio. Scope and non-claims This release does not claim: semantic understanding; cognition or consciousness; general-purpose compression superiority; universal corruption tolerance; production-readiness. It is a reproducible experimental baseline from which those structural questions can be tested more rigorously. Next directions reduce trail-symbol representation overhead; test long-lived incremental workloads and cross-file reuse; study relation lifetime and pruning without breaking stable IDs; evaluate structural retrieval and partial reconstruction; broaden independent corpora and hardware measurements; investigate adaptive protection policies under realistic storage-failure models.

title: The Intelligence Attractor Hypothesis: Independent Convergence Under Shared Reality Constraints
abstract: The Intelligence Attractor Hypothesis (IAH) proposes that independently formed intelligent systems approaching the best attainable performance under shared task, objective, context, and resource constraints may progressively lose functionally consequential differences attributable to their origins. The framework distinguishes Weak IAH, Strong IAH, Origin Attenuation, recursive architectural optimization, mutable system boundaries, and a separate maximal conjecture of architectural uniqueness. This version presents a conceptual hypothesis and research program; no empirical validation or formal peer review is claimed.

title: The Impact of Pedagogical Agents on Second Language Acquisition Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis Guided by Social Agency Theory
abstract: Digital Pedagogical Agents (DPAs) are virtual teaching entities created in the digital learning environment that have characteristics such as emotion and socialization. According to the basis of Social Agency Theory (SAT), a three-level random-effects meta-analytic model is employed in this paper to study the general effect and boundary conditions of DPAs in Second Language Acquisition (SLA) environments systematically. Through searches across seven Chinese and English databases, 31 independent empirical studies were identified, yielding 112 effect sizes (2002–2026). Based on the three-level random-effects model, the effect of DPA on SLA outcomes is about 0.607 (Hedges’ g = 0.607; 95% CI [0.45, 0.77]; p < 0.001), and there is a relatively large between-study heterogeneity. According to the moderation analysis, the magnitude of the effect varies greatly with different kinds of study designs, cultural contexts and learner characteristics, and although there is a moderating effect by publication type, it is not statistically significant. Funnel plot inspection, Egger’s test, and the trim-and-fill method all showed the presence of publication bias, yet the adjusted effect size remained robust (Hedges’ g = 0.521). This study provides quantitative evidence for understanding the mechanisms of DPAs in SLA and offers practical implications for instructional design and technological development in intelligent language learning environments.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography: Preparing for the Quantum Era
abstract: The emergence of quantum computing challenges the security of current cryptographic standards, mobilizing investigation and development of post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) schemes. We consider a unified approach for pre-quantum-proofing cryptographic infrastructure. It attempts to overcome these short comings and propose hybrid integration, optimized algorithm for resource constraint environment and secure migration. We focus on side-channel resistance, forward secrecy, and performance overhead in real-world application scenarios. We propose a common metric to evaluate quantum robustness. The goal of this work is to bridge the gap between theoretical PQC and scalable, enterprise-quality solutions.

title: Meticulously Unsupervised Entity Alignment With Large Language Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Knowledge graph entity alignment refers to the process of identifying and linking entities that refer to the same real‐world object from different knowledge graphs. Structural heterogeneity and scarcity of training data have always been two major challenges that impede entity alignment task. The advent of Large Language Models presents new avenues for entity knowledge completion and unsupervised EA, inspired by their extensive background knowledge and comprehensive capability to process semantic information. However, it is nontrivial to directly apply Large Language Models in addressing the aforementioned two challenges due to the following reasons: (1) it will blindly enrich entity knowledge in the absence of appropriate constraints; (2) as a probability based model, it could generate noisy labels that may mislead the alignment. To this end, this paper presents a novel unsupervised entity alignment framework, named LLM‐Align, to effectively leverage Large Language Models to precisely annotate entity pairs. First, Constrained Entity Information Enrichment (CIE) technique is devised, which employs attributes and relationships existing in the KGs to constrain the completion process, which alleviates structural heterogeneity between aligned entities. Subsequently, a Code‐formatted Prompt Template (CPT) module was designed to assist the Large Language Models in labelling entity pairs from candidates obtaining via both semantic and structural similarities. Ultimately, Combinatorial Optimization method based entity pair Refinement (COR) technique was conceived to further enhance the quality of the labelled entity pairs, which are used to train a base EA model. Extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the advantages of LLM‐Align.

title: VoT: Vision-of-Thought for Unified Multimodal Representation Alignment
abstract: Current text-to-image systems typically employ a "text encoder plus diffusion decoder" paradigm, in which text semantics directly modulate continuous latent noise. Despite their success, these methods lack an explicit, interpretable intermediate representation that effectively bridges high-level linguistic semantics and low-level visual signals. In this paper, we propose Vision-of-Thought (VoT), a framework that introduces a discrete visual-thinking layer between vision-language models (VLMs) and diffusion transformers (DiTs). Instead of treating VLMs merely as text encoders, we use them as multimodal planners that generate discrete VoT tokens representing high-level visual plans, such as objects and layouts, before rendering pixels. We train a specialized VoT tokenizer in the VLM semantic space with a closed-loop objective that combines VLM alignment, feature reconstruction, and vector-quantization losses. These objectives make the tokens semantically readable by the VLM while preserving the visual information needed for generation. Experimental results demonstrate that VoT improves semantic alignment and provides a structured interface for interpretable and controllable generation.

title: Quantile-Led Feature Extraction for Multi-Horizon Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Manufacturing Systems
abstract: In data-driven predictive maintenance (PdM), feature extraction is usually treated as fixed preprocessing: a descriptor set is chosen once and reused while the downstream model or forecasting horizon changes. This paper isolates the representation-learning stage and presents a quantile-led feature-extraction framework based on a dual-stage MLP-QRNN hierarchy. QRNN1 learns a broad ten-quantile conditional distribution for each sensor channel, while skip-connected QRNN2 refines a retained mid-tail quantile set into compact, channel-resolved, distribution-aware features. A fixed thirteen-pipeline ablation spans 1-hour, 70-hour, and 30-day regimes across 72 machines in 9 industrial facilities, with the downstream temporal classifier held fixed within each regime. Increasing the retained mid-tail set from two to four quantiles improves 30- and 60-minute F1-score, reaching 75.92% and 72.44% with attention enabled. The results also show that representations do not transfer reliably beyond their design horizon unless feature capacity, temporal embedding, activation strategy, and sensor breadth are scaled with the forecasting task. The unmodified short-horizon extractor falls to 42.90% F1 at 70 hours, whereas horizon-conditioned extractors reach 60.38% at 70 hours and 79.97% at 30 days. The framework therefore supports treating PdM feature extraction as a horizon-dependent representational stage rather than fixed preprocessing.

title: REFINE: Trajectory Representation Learning via Closed-Loop Transcription -- Extended Version
abstract: Trajectory representation learning underpins a wide range of trajectory analytics tasks; however, most existing self-supervised approaches, whether discriminative or generative, adopt an open-loop paradigm, relying on fixed data augmentations or random masking without feedback, which limits their ability to generalize and scale. We propose REFINE, a simple yet effective Representation lEarning Framework vIa closed-loop traNscription rEfinement for trajectory data. Drawing upon feedback control theory, REFINE tightly couples road-network-aware generative reconstruction with feedback-driven contrastive learning, enabling the model to capture fine-grained local movement semantics and global spatio-temporal dependencies without manually designed augmentation views. We further provide a control-theoretic analysis that establishes convergence guarantees for the proposed closed-loop optimization. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that REFINE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple downstream tasks while remaining computationally efficient and scalable. This paper is an extended version of REFINE: Trajectory Representation Learning via Closed-Loop Transcription, to appear in KDD 2026.
